provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The generator always builds a 5x1 column of five distinct colours. The output swaps cells 0 and 1 and swaps cells 3 and 4. The middle cell does not move. The rule ignores colour, so the palette has no effect on it.

Under D4, the column stays vertical when the clockwise rotation count is even. In that case the emitted program swaps the first two rows and the last two rows. When the rotation count is odd, the column becomes a 1x5 row. In that case the program swaps the first two columns and the last two columns.

The permutation is symmetric under reversing the line, because swapping both end pairs looks the same from either end. The row-reversal part of D4 indices 4 to 7 therefore needs no extra handling. Only the choice of axis has to be specialised.

The program works directly in visible coordinates and applies no normalisation, inverse transform or recolouring. It keeps the archived solver's behaviour for other lengths: the first pair is swapped when the length is at least 2, and the last pair when it is at least 4.
draft_notes.limitations: The generator only produces 5x1 grids, so the behaviour for other sizes is an extrapolation that mirrors the archived solver; the generator does not define it. The axis is fixed by d4 and is not inferred from the demonstrations. No constructor defects were found, and the fixtures match the rule exactly. I have not run any tests.
